title: Debar Blacklisted Construction Companies from Projects
what_it_is: Debar Blacklisted Construction Companies from Projects

sections.label: Demerit points and blacklisting
sections.summary: Companies with 25 demerit points are barred from hiring foreign workers; MOM issued about 2,400 points to 223 companies, debarring 25.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Second, companies that accumulate 25 demerit points are "blacklisted" by being barred from hiring foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Since the review in 2015, MOM has issued about 2,400 demerit points to 223 companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Twenty-five of these companies were debarred from hiring foreign workers.

sections.label: Construction fatalities reduced
sections.summary: The enhanced enforcement regime helped reduce construction workplace fatalities from 27 in 2015 to 24 in 2016 and four so far this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: With the enhanced enforcement regime, it has helped to reduce construction workplace fatalities from 27 in 2015 to 24 in 2016, and to four fatalities so far this year.

sections.label: PIE viaduct project award
sections.summary: When LTA awarded the PIE viaduct project to OKP in November 2015, the investigation into the September 2015 accident was still ongoing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: As explained by the Senior Minister of State for Transport just now, when LTA awarded the PIE viaduct project to OKP in November 2015, the investigation on the earlier September 2015 accident was still ongoing at the time.

sections.label: Strengthened BUS programme
sections.summary: In May 2016 the BUS programme was strengthened to put companies on BUS immediately after a fatal accident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: As part of the continual efforts to improve WSH performance, we have further strengthened our BUS programme in May 2016 to put companies on BUS immediately after a fatal accident.

sections.label: Fatality rates and deterrence
sections.summary: Fatality rates in the first seven months of 2017 fell to four cases, compared with 24 in 2016 and 27 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: As to the Member's second question on whether the current regime is tough enough to deter companies from taking short cuts and to infringe WSH practices, while we would like to think that the current regime is tough enough to deter companies, as Members can see, the fatality rates in the first seven months of 2017 had fallen remarkably to four fatality cases as compared to 24 for the whole of 2016, and 27 fatality cases in 2015.

sections.label: Companies under BUS surveillance
sections.summary: There are altogether 25 companies put under BUS surveillance so far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: With regard to the Member's second question on which are the companies that are put under BUS and are later on given the approval to exit, there are altogether 25 companies put under BUS surveillance so far.
